The cupid cichlid, Biotodoma cupido, is a geophagine cichlid from much of the Amazon basin, north to the Essequibo in Guyana and south to Bolivia.

Recorded throughout much of the Amazon basin, with its range extending eastwards from the Ucayali system in Peru as far as the Tocantins drainage which flows into the Atlantic alongside the Amazon at its delta.

Type locality is 'Rio Negro and Rio Guaporé, Mato Grosso, Brazil', the former located in Amazonas state, northwestern Brazil, and the latter a tributary of the rio Madeira basin in Mato Grosso state much further south.
Specimens from the vicinity of Iquitos in Peru can be easily recognized by the large, bronze- or copper-coloured spot that is exhibited by the male and that makes the fish very attractive.
